title: Lexicographically Smallest Negated Permutation that Sums to Target
summary: Given a positive integer n and an integer target, find the lexicographically smallest array of n integers where the sum equals the target and the absolute values of the elements are a permutation of 1 through n.
statement: Given a positive integer n and an integer target, find the lexicographically smallest array of n integers where the sum equals the target and the absolute values of the elements are a permutation of 1 through n. Return an empty array if no such array exists.
constraints: n is at most 100,000 and target has magnitude at most 10^10.
Absolute values must be a permutation of one through n and signed values must sum to target.
Return the lexicographically smallest valid array, or an empty list.
hints: Starting with all values positive gives total S; negating a subset of sum q changes the total to S-2q.
Feasibility requires q=(S-target)/2 to be an integer in [0,S].
Choose negative magnitudes greedily from n downward whenever the remaining sum is achievable by smaller values, then sort the positive remainder.
This maximizes the earliest negative magnitude lexicographically, while consecutive integers can realize every residual sum through their triangular capacity.
editorial: This maximizes the earliest negative magnitude lexicographically, while consecutive integers can realize every residual sum through their triangular capacity.

tests.explanation: Choosing negative three and positive one and two yields the smallest array [-3,1,2].
The target lies outside the possible sum range, so no array exists.
